Thanks Elliot — great details and the sample file is helpful. High-level recommendation first, then suggested pilot sizing and fallback policy:

1) Recommendation (short):
- H100: use for your long-context chat (32k windows) and RLHF-style samplers where memory bandwidth and NVLink matter.
- A100 (40GB/80GB as appropriate): memory-first for sessions that need large KV caches but where FP16/AMP is fine; cheaper than H100 for similar memory footprints.
- L4: cost-effective for embeddings, short-context classification, and as a low-latency tier for S1/preview users.

2) Pilot sizing (POC, 6-week):
- Start with a small multi-tier pool: 4x H100 (for 32k hot set + cache warmers), 6x A100-80GB (memory headroom for 8k contexts with larger batches), 12x L4 (high QPS embedding & low-latency).
- Reserve ~60% of the H100 pool for steady-state, leave 40% as burstable (dedicated burst slots or on-demand).

3) Fallback / resiliency pattern:
- Route by policy: latency-critical chat -> prefer H100; if H100 unavailable, fallback to A100 with conservative decoding params (max_tokens -20%, top_p lower) and a customer-facing banner for increased latency.
- For embeddings, prefer L4; if L4 exhausted, overflow to A100 using quantized kernels (4-bit) to preserve throughput.
- Use prefix caching aggressively for chat starter prompts to reduce recomputation on H100.

4) Cost & ops notes:
- H100 gives best p50 latency on long context but highest $/hr. Consider model quantization + transformer-fused kernels to lower per-token cost.
- A100 often best bang-for-memory when you need large KV caches but can accept slightly higher latency than H100.
- L4 is excellent for QPS-heavy parts; plan for horizontal scaling and autoscale policies that prioritize L4 for embeddings.

I'll attach a short SKU tradeoff matrix and a proposed mutual action plan. Ben, can you add ops/SLAs and suggest a reserve/burst pricing split?

Best,

Quick ops addendum — diving into the numbers you sent.

POC assumptions (derived from cascade_mvp_workload_samples.csv):
- 95th percentile QPS for embeddings: ~450 qps (512 tokens)
- Chat steady-state: ~80 concurrent sessions, peak 250 with long contexts (8k-32k)
- Nightly batch: 2M tokens over a 3-hour window

Suggested slotting & capacity hedges:
- H100 (4 nodes): provision for 40 concurrent long-context sessions with KV caching; assume 2.5x overhead for cache hot-warm transitions. Plan a canary with 1 replica per AZ.
- A100-80GB (6 nodes): backfill long-context overflow and run batch rerank workers; configure preemptible burst pool to 2 nodes (for cost-smoothing).
- L4 (12 nodes): autoscale to 30k concurrency for embeddings; use token-based throttling and per-customer QPS caps.

Fallthrough policy (automated):
- If H100 queue > 75% for 30s, circuit-break to A100 with conservative decoding settings and enable fast-KV-eviction to limit memory pressure.
- If A100 and L4 both saturated for embeddings, queue non-critical jobs and send back pressure to clients with retry-after headers.

Telemetry & SLOs to include in contract:
- P50/P95 latency per model per SKU, token-rate per second, cache hit ratio, and API error rate.
- Include a 5% monthly credit if P95 chat latency exceeds 2.5x target for more than 3 days in a month.

Pricing split for POC (ballpark):
- Reserve commit: 60% of steady usage across H100/A100; 40% burst (on-demand or preemptible). We can trade committed discount vs. burst multiplier — I recommend a 1.4x burst premium cap for the POC.

I'll put these into the mutual_action_plan doc and flag ops for a canary run window.

-ben

Aisha / Elliot — thanks for the constraints. Summary action items and an alternate low-cost pilot:

Alternate low-cost pilot (to meet ~$75k/mo commit):
- H100: 2 nodes (hot path only) — reserved for the enterprise 32k flows and one canary; aggressive KV caching to limit node count.
- A100-40GB: 4 nodes (fallback & batch) — use mixed-precision + 4-bit quantization when acceptable; will support overflow from H100.
- L4: 10 nodes (embeddings + most short-context chat) — scale horizontally, keep warm-cache pools.
- Reserve/burst plan: reserve ~55% steady usage, allow burst via on-demand capped at 1.6x with monthly cap and clear rollback policy.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: longer P95 latency for edge long-context traffic when H100 saturates. Mitigation: automatic decoding parameter reduction + customer-visible latency notice + priority routing for key enterprise customers.
- Risk: memory pressure on A100-40GB for some 32k-derived KV states. Mitigation: fall back to segmented KV (streamed KV chunks) and offload embeddings cache to a fast in-memory store.

Next steps (mutual action plan):
1) We will share SOC2 evidence by EOD tomorrow (Irene looping infra/security).
2) Ben & Ops to finalize telemetry SLOs and canary run dates (ops will propose Nov 16–20 window).
3) I will update the mutual_action_plan.docx with the low-cost pilot numbers and pricing estimate; Camila to share a HubSpot deal link and DocuSign stub for signature.

Elliot / Aisha — if that looks good I will schedule a 30-min review to finalize reserve numbers and SLA language.
